No, Albert Einstein did not fail math in school. In fact, he was a very good student and often struggled with physical education, which was his favorite subject during high school. However, he excelled in mathematics and physics, and his intelligence and curiosity eventually led him to become one of the most renowned physicists of all time.

Einstein's academic achievements were impressive. He attended Swiss secondary schools and then enrolled at the Swiss Federal Polytechnic University in Zurich, where he studied civil engineering for a year before switching to physics. He graduated from the university in 1900 with a degree in physics.

Einstein's struggles in math were actually quite common among his peers, especially those who would later become famous scientists like him. Many people at the time believed that if you were intelligent and talented, you should pursue a career in science or mathematics, regardless of your aptitude for these subjects. However, Einstein proved them wrong by persevering through challenges and eventually becoming one of the greatest minds in history.

It's worth noting that the phrase "failed math" is likely an oversimplification, as it implies that he never had any interest in math or was somehow unable to succeed there. In reality, Einstein showed a strong aptitude for mathematics from an early age, and his academic record reflects his exceptional abilities rather than any difficulties he may have faced.
